subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmehealth.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Tom and Sofia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Production latency spikes during morning surge (7–10am PT) causing timeouts on patient-facing summarization features.
- Current per-request costs on cloud endpoints are unpredictable at scale; forecasting is difficult for monthly budget committees.
- Data isolation requirement: PHI needs to remain in your VPC with strict audit logs and KMS-managed keys.

Goals you outlined:
- Stable p99 latency <= 250ms for 512-token generation for clinical summaries.
- Predictable monthly spend for budget approval (targeting < $X, to be finalized with usage numbers).
- Dedicated, isolated GPU capacity with KMS integration and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Redwood Dedicated proposal (high-level):
- Reserved pool: 8x A100-80GB equiv GPUs (reserved capacity) to cover peak throughput with autoscaling buffer.
- Isolation: Private cluster in your VPC with customer-managed KMS keys and audit-log streaming to your Splunk bucket.
- Scaling plan: 2x burst capacity policy for short spikes + scheduled scaling window for mornings. Continuous prefix cache to reduce generator cost on repeated prompts.
- SLA targets: 99.5% uptime on serving endpoints; P99 latency SLO of 250ms for configured 512-token profile (we’ll run a short soak to validate).

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft SOW (Dedicated_Capacity_SOW_v1.pdf) and a preliminary capacity estimate workbook (capacity-estimates-acme-20260420.xlsx) with traffic assumptions.

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) Your team to confirm traffic profile (sample QPS distribution) — see the spreadsheet tab “Traffic Input.”
2) Redwood to run a 2-week validation soak on a dedicated dev cluster to validate p99 latency and cost estimates.
3) Follow-on meeting with procurement/legal to review SOW and SOC2 artifacts — suggest Wed 29 Apr.

If that looks right, I’ll loop in a technical kickoff invite and ask Rishi to share preliminary pricing ranges.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

2) Regarding the 8x A100 estimate: can Rishi include a 6x and 10x cost option so procurement can see the sensitivity?

Hi all — quick pricing note as requested. Assumptions: 30-day month; expected avg utilization during peak window ~70% for reserved pool. Burst capacity charged at on-demand uplift rate.

Estimated monthly cost (incl. infra + support):
- 6x A100 equiv: $62,000/mo
- 8x A100 equiv: $79,000/mo (recommended for peak safety margin)
- 10x A100 equiv: $94,000/mo

We’ll include a line item for the 2-week validation soak (one-time charge) and a discount ladder for 12/24-month commitments. I’ll attach a formal pricing deck to the HubSpot deal and send updated SOW draft to Laura for redline.

-Rishi
